steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three major, widely cited causes of World War I:

1. Alliance System and Entangling Treaties  
   • By 1914 Europe was divided into two rival blocs—the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia).  
   • A local conflict risked drawing in every partner because members had pledged mutual support. When Austria-Hungary moved against Serbia, alliances rapidly pulled the great powers into general war.

2. Militarism and the Arms Race  
   • All the great powers had been expanding armies, navies, and weapons budgets for decades.  
   • Germany and Britain, in particular, raced to out-build one another’s fleets (e.g., Dreadnought battleships). This produced a climate in which military options seemed attractive and mobilization timetables were rigid.

3. Nationalism and Imperial Rivalries  
   • Ethnic groups in the Balkans sought independence or expansion (Serbs, Bulgarians, Croats), threatening Austria-Hungary’s stability.  
   • Major powers competed for colonies and prestige—Germany resented France and Britain’s larger empires, while France wanted revenge for losing Alsace-Lorraine to Germany in 1871.  
   • National pride made compromise difficult and encouraged public support for war when crises arose.

(Other contributing factors often listed include the immediate spark of the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914, economic rivalries, and failures of diplomacy.)
